subject: Temporary analytics routing + APAC subprocessor roster and DPA addendum
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@aperturehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@aphealth.com
Date: 2026-12-01T08:14:00-08:00
Subject: Quick question on short-term analytics routing to US + APAC subprocessor list

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Aperture liked the latency profile on the dedicated pool. We have a couple of compliance items before the legal team will sign:

1) We need written confirmation on whether Redwood can permit a brief (up to 72h) analytics sync from our APAC data slice to the US for a planned ETL job during a maintenance window. This would be temporary for a one-off migration and must be limited to aggregated telemetry only (no PII).

2) Please provide an up-to-date APAC subprocessor roster (including country, vendor name, and purpose) and confirmation that any APAC subprocessors will not persist customer content outside the region beyond the stated 72h window.

3) We may require a narrow DPA addendum clause that codifies short-term temporary cross-border processing for emergency maintenance/failover. Can you send a draft or indicate if Redwood can sign our standard addendum?

Attaching our internal checklist would help — procurement looped in. Can you get back to us by EOD Dec 3? This is blocking a scheduled rollout.

Best,
Emma
Director, Security & Privacy
Aperture Health

Attachments referenced: Aperture_Compliance_Checklist.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-02T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick question on short-term analytics routing to US + APAC subprocessor list

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers up front, then details:

- Yes, we can support a one-off temporary analytics sync (up to 72 hours) for aggregated telemetry only, provided Aperture signs a short DPA addendum covering scope and retention.
- I attached our APAC subprocessor roster and a draft addendum that limits the processing window and requires deletion proof within 7 days.

Details:
- Routing: We can route the job through our US analytics cluster as a controlled job with explicit tags. The job will be limited to aggregated metrics and will be run under a scoped service account with logging.
- Isolation & deletion: We will ensure any derived outputs stored in US buckets are auto-deleted after 7 days. We will provide a deletion report (object list + timestamps) as evidence.
- KMS/keys: If you need customer-managed keys (CMKs) for the transient artifacts, we support bringing your keys via AWS KMS. We can also use our managed keys and provide key-use logs.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the attached "Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf" (draft) — it includes a Temporary Cross-Border Processing exhibit.
2) We confirm the exact timeframe and tagging for the ETL job.
3) We sign the addendum and schedule a short compliance call (30 min) to walk through prove-out steps.

Looping Laura (Legal) and Sean (Sales Ops) to confirm routing playbook and timelines.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf, subprocessor_roster_APAC.csv
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-03T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft temp cross-border clause — legal notes

Ben / Sean — I reviewed Ben's draft addendum. High-level comments:

- Scope: Good to explicitly enumerate "aggregated telemetry" and add examples (counts, latency histograms). Exclude any document-level or user-level content by name or id.
- Retention & audit: 7-day auto-delete acceptable, but Ops must provide a signed deletion manifest within 14 days (manifest + checksum).
- Binding conditions: Add a clause that temp processing is allowed only if Redwood's smart-routing is used (no manual exports). That prevents ad-hoc downloads.
- Subprocessor liability: For the APAC roster, ensure subprocessors are bound by the same DPA terms and confirm they will not retain copies post-deletion. We should require subprocessors to provide a deletion confirmation as well.

Operational ask for Sean / Ops: can we commit to object-level deletion manifests and provide logs with KMS key IDs? If not, we need to push retention to 14 days.

I'll prepare a redlined PDF and a one-paragraph summary for the customer.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-04T15:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Draft temp cross-border clause — ops confirmation

Laura / Ben — ops can meet the proposed guarantees with one caveat: object-level deletion manifests are supported, but producing a signed checksum for every object requires an extra step in our workflow. We can do the following without infra changes:

- Create a timeboxed job that writes the transient objects to a pre-provisioned S3 bucket in the US account with server-side encryption (either customer CMK or our RMK).
- After deletion, we can export a manifest that contains object paths, deletion timestamps, and the KMS key id. We can also include MD5 checksums for objects up to 50MB; for larger objects we will include size + deletion timestamp.
- Ops will run the job under a locked service account and capture CloudTrail events for the operation window.

If the customer insists on cryptographic signatures over each manifest (signed by Redwood legal), we can provide that as a manual step (signed PDF) after the fact.

We can meet the 7-day deletion window if legal accepts the hybrid checksum approach above. Otherwise, we recommend the 14-day window to avoid any manual post-processing.

I'll draft the operations playbook and send to you both by EOD Dec 6.

—Sean
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Emma Li <emma.li@aperturehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aphealth.com
Date: 2026-12-15T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Temporary analytics routing + APAC subprocessor roster and DPA addendum

Ben / Laura — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the clarity on operational controls. Aperture accepts the hybrid manifest approach with the following asks before we execute:

1) Add a short sentence in the addendum that Redwood will provide the deletion manifest (object paths, deletion timestamps, KMS key id, MD5 where available) within 14 days of the job completion.
2) Include the APAC roster CSV as an exhibit to the addendum (we need vendor contact for each entry).
3) We'll want DocuSign for the addendum — please send final redline, and procurement will countersign the DPA addendum and return.

If you can send the final addendum and a signed manifest template by Dec 17 we will approve the window and book the maintenance slot for Dec 21-22.

Appreciate you and the ops team making this straightforward.

Best,
Emma
Director, Security & Privacy
Aperture Health

Forwarded attachment references: Aperture_Compliance_Checklist.pdf (from initial mail)
